summary: Matthew B. Orsborn completed his PhD at the University of Hong Kong in 2012 under Guang Xing and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa, and studied under traditional teachers Hsing Yun and Huishang. In 2026, he is attested as Professor and Head of International Affairs at the Chung-Hwa Institute.
Specializing in Indology and religious studies, Matthew Clark completed his PhD at SOAS University of London between 1999 and 2004. During his studies, he was taught by Daud Ali and George Botterill.
Active in Buddhist studies and sociology, Matthew Immergut studied under Culadasa. In 2011, he is attested as Associate Professor of Sociology at Purchase College, State University of New York.

Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Matthew MacKenzie completed an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa between 1996 and 2004. In 2008, he held a post as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Colorado State University.

A scholar of Indology and religious studies, Matthew R. Sayers earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2008) under Joel Peter Brereton and Patrick Olivelle. He held a post at Lebanon Valley College, attested in 2013.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Japanology, Mitchell studied at Osaka City University, the Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies, UH Mānoa (MA, under Helen Baroni and Michel Mohr), and Duke University (PhD, attested 2015, under Richard M. Jaffe).

Kapstein earned a PhD at Brown (1980–1987) under Chisholm, Quinn, and Van Cleve, and studied with several Tibetan masters. He held positions at the University of Chicago (1986, 1996, 1998), Columbia University (~1989–1996), and EPHE (2002).
Active in Indology and linguistics, Matthew Thomson Adam served as a missionary teacher for the London Missionary Society from 1820 to 1830 and taught at Presidency University until 1830.

A specialist in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, Matthew W. King earned his PhD at the University of Toronto in 2014 under Frances Garrett. He also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab and Thubten Champa.

Matthias Alexander Castrén (1813–1852) specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki and the Imperial Alexander University (~1830–1836) and held posts at both institutions from around 1851 to 1852.

Matthias Christian Sprengel (1746–1803) studied at Rostock, Bützow, and Göttingen (under August Ludwig von Schlözer). He became an extraordinary professor of history at Göttingen in 1778 and was University Librarian at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1778 to 1801.

Matthias Hermanns (1899–1972) studied at Missionshaus St. Gabriel, Vienna (under Wilhelm Schmidt and Wilhelm Koppers), and Fribourg (PhD ~1946–1948). He taught at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1950–1954), and the Steyler Missionswissenschaftliches Institut (1960–1968).
Matthias de Vries (1820–1892) was a linguist who studied at Leiden University (~1837–1843). He held academic posts at the University of Groningen (1849–1853) and Leiden University (1853–1891).

Matthias von Lexer (1830–1892) studied at Graz, Vienna, Berlin, and Erlangen-Nuremberg (PhD ~1859–1860) under scholars including Bopp and Weber. He held professorships at the universities of Freiburg (1863, 1866), Würzburg (1868), and Munich (1890).

Matthieu Ricard studied molecular biology at the Pasteur Institute under François Jacob (doctorate ~1967–1972) and trained under traditional teachers Kangyur Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He co-founded Karuna-Shechen and joined the Mind and Life Institute board in 2000.

Mattia Salvini studied at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College and earned a PhD in Buddhist philosophy from SOAS under Tadeusz Skorupski. He held posts at the International Buddhist College and Mahidol University (attested 2015).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics, Mauli Chand Prasad completed his doctoral dissertation at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University under B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna. In 1984, he was attested as Lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.
Maureen L. P. Patterson (1930–2019) worked in Indology and was a student of W. Norman Brown. She served as South Asia Librarian at the University of Chicago, attested in 1984 and 2007.

Maurice Bloomfield (1855–1928) studied at Chicago, Furman, Yale, Johns Hopkins (PhD ~1878–1879 under Charles Rockwell Lanman), and in Germany. He served as professor at Johns Hopkins University from 1881 to 1926.

Maurice Grammont (1866–1946) studied at EPHE and the University of Paris (PhD, 1895) under Saussure, Bréal, Schmidt, and Thurneysen. He was Maître de conférences at Burgundy (1892–1895) and Professor of Comparative Linguistics at Montpellier (1895–1939).
